messages.content:
The failing test `testRevert` in the `LineTest` class creates a `Line` object with two `Vector3D` objects as parameters, calculates the expected direction by negating the direction of the line, then calls the `revert` method on the line and compares the direction of the reverted line with the expected direction using `assertArrayEquals`.

The current bug report mentions that the `revert` method in the `Line` class only maintains around 10 digits for the direction, causing issues when evaluating the line's position far from the origin. The report suggests using `Vector3D.negate()` for the direction as a simple fix and questions why `Line` is not immutable when it's composed of two vectors.

By looking at the code snippet of the `revert` method in the `Line` class, we can see that the direction of the reverted line is calculated by subtracting the direction from the zero vector. This implementation may lead to precision issues as mentioned in the bug report.

To fix this issue, we should update the `revert` method in the `Line` class to use `Vector3D.negate()` for calculating the direction of the reverted line.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
The best locations to fix this issue would be:
```
org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line.revert()
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
